roll.7:
7 May 2023: Caroline attended an LGBTQ support group. Hearing trans stories made her feel accepted, grateful, and courageous. Shared photo of a dog beside a mural of a woman.

8 May: Caroline planned to pursue education/counseling work supporting others; Melanie praised her empathy. Melanie shared a sunset-lake painting; painting helps her relax and express feelings. Caroline researched career options; Melanie planned a swim with her kids.

20 May: Melanie ran in a mental-health charity race.

25 May: Melanie said the race underscored mental health and self-care; she tried to run, read, and play violin daily. Her kids anticipated summer; family considered June camping. Caroline researched LGBTQ-friendly adoption agencies and hoped to give children a loving home, though single parenting felt daunting. Shared sign/building photo; Melanie encouraged her.

9 June: Caroline spoke at school about her trans journey and inclusion. She began transitioning after coming out three years earlier. Friends, family, and mentors were her “rocks” after a breakup; shared photo with friends. Melanie said her husband and kids motivated her; shared family, wedding, and outing photos; she had been married five years.

27 June: Caroline’s Swedish grandmother’s cross-heart necklace represented faith, family, and roots; she treasured a bowl made by a friend for her 18th birthday. Melanie shared bowl photos; her family camped in the mountains. Caroline attended an LGBTQ counseling workshop and hoped to support trans people.

3 July: Caroline attended a pride parade, learned about advocacy, considered counseling, was learning piano, and planned to attend a transgender conference. Melanie took pottery classes and made a flower-patterned bowl.

6 July: Caroline continued exploring mental-health work and built a children’s library with classics, multicultural, and educational books (shared photo). Melanie took her kids to a museum; they loved the dinosaur exhibit (shared water-play photo). Her childhood favorite book was “Charlotte’s Web” (shared cover photo). Caroline picnicked with friends (shared photo) and credited her support network with love, guidance, and acceptance through transition. Melanie shared a family beach-campfire photo.

12 July: Caroline said she had attended an LGBTQ conference on 10 July; meeting people with similar journeys felt welcoming and affirming. It strengthened her gratitude for community and desire to fight for trans rights and raise awareness. She was still researching counseling/mental-health careers, motivated by her own mental-health struggles and the support she received. Melanie encouraged her and shared a photo of a book cover with a gold coin; Caroline said books guide and motivate her and help her understand herself. Her favorite was “Becoming Nicole” by Amy Ellis Nutt, a true story about a trans girl and her family; it gave her connection and hope. She took from it self-acceptance, seeking support, and the belief that hard times pass and hope and love exist. Caroline also remarked that pets bring joy. Melanie shared photos of two little girls with a dog and a cat; she has a dog and cat named Luna and Oliver (which pet has which name not specified). They brighten the household and are sweet and playful. Melanie shared photos of new pink/purple running shoes, said she had been running farther since their last chat to de-stress and clear her mind, and planned to continue because it improved her mental health.
roll.13:
7 May 2023: Caroline attended an LGBTQ support group; trans people’s stories made her feel accepted, grateful, courageous. Shared dog/mural photo.

May–June: Caroline considered education/counseling, researched LGBTQ-friendly adoption, and hoped to give children a loving home, though solo parenting felt daunting. Melanie praised her empathy; ran for mental-health charity and tried running, reading, violin. Caroline spoke at school about transition (came out three years earlier) and inclusion. Supportive friends, family, mentors helped after breakup. Melanie had been married five years; husband/kids motivate her.

June–August: Caroline values trans advocacy, Pride, LGBTQ community; treasures necklace from Swedish grandmother and friend-made bowl. Explored counseling, piano, children’s library. Favorite book *Becoming Nicole*; favorite color blue. Joined youth mentorship, mentored a trans teen; June Pride with mentee was a highlight. Uses art to express identity and promote acceptance; “Embracing Identity” explores self-acceptance. Melanie enjoys art, pottery, family, camping, beach, running; childhood favorite *Charlotte’s Web*. Pets Luna and Oliver (which is which unclear). Melanie’s favorite memories include Perseids and family milestones. They recalled last year’s Pride fest and planned a summer outing.

23 Aug: Caroline applied to adoption agencies after attending an adoption-advice group; excited and nervous. Her guinea pig Oscar loves parsley. Melanie has pets including Oliver and new cat Bailey; Oliver once hid a bone in her slipper. Caroline rode horses with her dad as a child; Melanie paints horses. Caroline’s blue-faced self-portrait made her feel liberated and empowered. Art, supportive people, LGBTQ advocacy, and authentic living matter to her.
roll.19:
Caroline is transgender; came out around 2020. Values authenticity, LGBTQ+ advocacy, Pride, and supportive community. An LGBTQ group on 7 May 2023 helped her feel accepted and courageous. Friends, family, and mentors supported her after a breakup and through transition. Spoke at school about transition/inclusion; considered counseling, children’s library work, and LGBTQ-friendly adoption. Applied to adoption agencies in Aug 2023, excited but nervous about solo parenting. Mentors a trans teen and volunteers at an LGBTQ youth center; Pride with mentee was a highlight. Planned youth talent/art shows for Sep 2023. Guinea pig Oscar loves parsley.

Art expresses identity and acceptance; began around age 17. Works include stained-glass “Embracing Identity,” rainbow mural, eagle, and red/blue painting challenging gender binaries. Likes drawing flowers; favorite color blue, book *Becoming Nicole*. Treasures Swedish grandmother’s necklace and friend-made bowl. Rode horses with dad; plays acoustic guitar since around 2018. Meaningful song: “Brave” by Sara Bareilles.

Melanie was married five years by 2023; husband and children motivate her. Enjoys art, pottery, camping, beach, running, music; paints landscapes, still lifes, horses. Played clarinet since childhood; favorite childhood book *Charlotte’s Web*. Pets Bailey, Luna, Oliver; Oliver hid a bone in her slipper. Ran for mental-health charity; likes Bach, Mozart, and Ed Sheeran’s “Perfect.”

28 Aug 2023: Melanie took kids to park; Caroline volunteered; Melanie attended Summer Sounds. 13 Sep: Caroline biked with friends and shared beach sunset; Melanie shared camping forest road. Caroline said volunteering inspires her heart painting. Melanie has made art seven years and shared pottery; Caroline was open to trying pottery. Some friends rejected Caroline’s transition; supportive current ties feel genuine. Melanie shared café-door sign as precaution.

13 Oct: Caroline sought mentor’s adoption advice and felt ready to offer children a safe home. She advised Melanie to research agencies/lawyers, gather documents/references, and prepare for waiting. Melanie’s friend adopted in 2022, inspiring her interest. Melanie recovering from Sep injury, paused pottery; read Caroline’s book and painted a calming pink sunset and abstract blue streaks. Caroline recently tried abstract art. On 6 Oct Caroline attended trans poetry reading; shared classroom poster, “Trans Lives Matter” sign, and woman-in-dress drawing representing freedom/womanhood.

20 Oct 2023: Melanie recounted car accident on road trip; son was okay, children scared but reassured. Accident made her cherish family, her main support and motivation. Family enjoyed Grand Canyon; shared photo of kids overlooking canyon. Next day walked trail; shared photo of woman and child. Camping brings presence, bonding through stories/campfires, peaceful nature, birds, fresh air; shared waterside sunset.

22 Oct 2023: Caroline passed adoption agency interviews the previous Friday (20 Oct), a major step toward having a family. Melanie congratulated her and shared photo of two wooden dolls, saying they reminded her of family love; asked Caroline’s future vision. Caroline hopes to give children without a home a safe, loving, accepting family; sees adoption as giving back. They discussed self-acceptance, Caroline’s difficult transition, and how support from friends, family, and mentors helped her find herself; she wants to pass that support on. Melanie praised her strength and inspiration; both value being there for one another. Caroline shared photos of a green/yellow-design clock and a painting with “happiness” written on it; said living honestly and being oneself is freeing.

rebuild.7:
Caroline: Swedish, transgender; transitioning since ~June 2020. Friends (known since moving from home country ~2019), family, mentors supported her, especially after a difficult breakup. LGBTQ group (May 7, 2023), pride parade (week of June 26–July 2), and conferences (July 10; planned another in July) brought belonging and inspired advocacy. Spoke at a school about her journey (week before June 9), encouraging allies. Exploring counseling/mental-health work, especially supporting trans people; attended LGBTQ counseling workshop June 23. Support groups helped her mental health and self-acceptance. Plans single-parent adoption; researching LGBTQ-inclusive agencies as of May 25, aiming to give children a safe, loving home. Building a future children’s library. Learning piano; loves reading. Favorite book: *Becoming Nicole* (Amy Ellis Nutt); also likes *Charlotte’s Web*’s message (Melanie’s childhood favorite). Keeps grandmother’s cross-and-heart necklace from Sweden and a friend’s hand-painted bowl (18th birthday, ~2017).

Melanie: married ~2018; husband and children motivate her. Self-care includes running, reading, violin; running farther by July 12 improved her mental health. Painted lake sunrise (2022); pottery class from July 2, made black-and-white flower bowl; pottery is therapeutic and meaningful. Ran mental-health charity race May 20. Took children swimming (May 8), museum July 5 (dinosaur exhibit), and mountain camping (week before June 27); family also loves beach camping. Children anticipated summer break; considered June camping. Has dog and cat, Luna and Oliver (which is which unknown). Proud of Caroline’s advocacy. Melanie shared family photos, but pictured identities aren’t confirmed.
rebuild.13:

She values authenticity, blue (relaxing), faith/family roots (grandmother’s cross-and-heart necklace), and her friend’s hand-painted bowl. LGBTQ groups, counseling and pride events gave her belonging and inspired advocacy. She mentors a trans teen and joined Connected LGBTQ Activists. Interested in counseling/mental health to support trans people; attended a workshop 23 Jun 2023. Pursuing single-parent adoption to provide a loving home; researching agencies, attended a council meeting 14 Jul, applied in Aug. Loves books (“Becoming Nicole,” favorite; also “Charlotte’s Web” childhood favorite), piano and art. Her art explores identity/inclusion; paintings include “Embracing Identity,” a tree/sun, and a blue-faced self-portrait. Planned an August art show.

Melanie: married about 2018, has husband and children; family is central. Loves camping, hiking, beach trips, nature, running, reading, violin, painting and pottery. Pets include dog and cat Luna/Oliver; also Bailey and Oliver; Caroline has guinea pig Oscar. Melanie’s art is therapeutic. Caroline and Melanie are supportive friends; attended Pride together in 2022. Melanie’s family camping memories include Perseid meteors (2022). Melanie ran a mental-health charity race (20 May 2023); took children to museum (5 Jul) and pottery workshop (14 Jul). Caroline attended Pride 11 Aug 2023; Melanie went to Matt Patterson concert for daughter’s birthday (13 Aug).
rebuild.19:
Caroline (surname unknown) is a transgender woman from Sweden, transitioning since about 2020. Friends, family, mentors, and LGBTQ community support helped her accept herself; she advocates, makes art about identity, volunteers with LGBTQ youth, mentors a trans teen, and belongs to Connected LGBTQ Activists. Art, reading, guitar (since ~2018), and piano matter to her; favorite book is *Becoming Nicole*. She explores counseling/mental-health work to help others. She attended LGBTQ events and a trans poetry reading in 2023.

Caroline has long wanted to adopt and give children a safe, loving home. She researched LGBTQ-inclusive agencies, applied in August 2023, sought mentor advice (Oct 13), and passed agency interviews Oct 20. She hopes to adopt children without prior homes.

Melanie is married (about 2018) with children; family is her main support and motivation. They enjoy camping, hiking, beaches, museums, and art. Melanie paints and does pottery; running, reading, violin, and clarinet help her self-care. She has pets Luna, Oliver, and Bailey (which names correspond to which pets is unclear); Caroline has guinea pig Oscar. Melanie’s son was in a road-trip accident Oct 14–15, 2023, but was okay; family visited Grand Canyon. Caroline and Melanie are supportive friends.
